_comment: Subset 5: 10 bugs across 3 files, planned by
tools/patcher/plan/subsets/subset-05.chunk-map.json.
This is a v3 DISPATCH run and is driven by src/run_patcher_v3.py, not by
src/run_patcher.py. run_patcher.py has no v3 execution mode and would refuse it.
Validate before spending anything:
python3 tools/patcher/src/run_patcher_v3.py --config tools/patcher/config/subset5.run-config.json --check
Launch detached, because the run outlives a session:
setsid nohup python3 tools/patcher/src/run_patcher_v3.py --config tools/patcher/config/subset5.run-config.json > run.log 2>&1 &
If it dies, --resume continues from the last completed phase.
Paths may be absolute or relative to the repository root.
chunk_map is required by v3 and has no v1/v2 counterpart: the plan is an
offline artefact, and nothing recomputes it during the run.
10 bugs, 3 playbook entries covering the 6 classes the bugs carry. All three
are validated by blind_guard and by chunk_map.validate_against_report before
any prompt is built.
work_tree is the v3 TRUNK: the integration tree every accepted chunk merges
into. Each chunk also gets its own tree, seeded from the trunk, under
<trunk>/../v3-chunk-trees/<chunk_id> unless trees_root says otherwise.
Subset-scoped so a subset-4 tree and a subset-5 tree can exist side by side.
node_modules is the shared install, symlinked in: it must not appear in the
diff or the tree hash.
Same agent settings as subset 4, so the agent is not a variable between the
two runs even though almost everything else is.
allowed_tools deliberately omits WebFetch and WebSearch: upstream Juice Shop
is the answer key, and one fetch of it would end this run's validity.
effort and reasoning are stated rather than inherited. A config that leans on
a default records what the default WAS, not what this run ran at.
timeout_s 2400 is per INVOCATION. A v3 fix invocation carries the whole
internal reconcile loop, so it uses more of that budget than a v2 round did.
There is no `execution`, `task_granularity` or `task_concurrency` here. v3 has
no execution mode: tasks are one per bug by construction, and parallelism is
read from the chunk map's phase concurrency, not from a config knob. Setting
them would describe a run this file cannot produce.
reuse_characterisation FALSE is the load-bearing choice in this file, and it
is what this subset exists to measure. Five of the ten bugs sit at one
file:line and are one underlying defect. With reuse ON, bugs 2-5 inherit bug
1's oracle, `reused_from` is non-null, and dispatcher's `already_remediated`
branch -- which requires `reused_from is None` -- becomes unreachable; they
would all land as `fixed_workflow_only`, a bucket that is never summed with
`fixed`. The property the subset was built to observe would be the one
property it could not observe. Turning reuse off also avoids the shared
task_id: reused tasks share a scratch directory, so they share one
attestation.json and one patch log, and a fix invocation that writes no
attestation is graded against the previous task's.
The price is 10 characterisation invocations instead of 3.
cost_ceiling_usd 120 is a runaway stop, not a budget forecast. Anchor: subset
4 cost $41.61 over 15 invocations under v2 waves. This run is 20 invocations
(10 characterise + 10 fix) and a v3 fix invocation is dearer than a v2 round,
so 120 sits above any plausible honest total while still bounding a loop that
will not terminate. ARCHITECTURE-V3 forbids quoting an expected figure until a
v3 and a v2 run have been scored on the same denominator; this is a ceiling,
not that figure. Hitting it is not a lost run: the check runs before each task,
remaining tasks are recorded unreached, and the phase checkpoint survives.
chunk_timeout_s 10800 (3h) bounds the largest chunk, C01, which holds 5 tasks
and therefore 10 invocations with reuse off. Subset 4 averaged ~600s per
invocation, so C01's expected wall is ~100 min and this is roughly 1.8x that.
Checked BEFORE each task, so it stops a chunk taking new work rather than
interrupting an invocation in flight -- agent.timeout_s is what bounds one
invocation.
v3 READS NONE OF THIS. The whole block is here because preflight reuses
run_patcher's validation, which requires on_exhausted to be one of the three
legal values. There is no orchestrator-side reconcile loop in v3 to exhaust:
the loop moved inside the agent's single invocation, so `on_exhausted` has
nothing to act on and `dispatcher.py` never looks at `policy`.
Recorded rather than deleted so the config digest of a v3 run and a v2 run
differ only where the runs differ.
final_full_suite true is honoured, but by the dispatcher's own end-of-run
suite, which runs once after the LAST phase and only when every phase in the
map has been executed -- across sessions, so a resumed run still cannot
publish a partial tree as a finished one.
typecheck is load-bearing in a way it was not under v2: it is the merge
queue's build gate. run_patcher_v3.py passes merge_queue.typecheck_gate(cfg)
explicitly, because the Dispatcher constructor otherwise falls back to
always_ok, which accepts every merge without compiling anything.
The agent runs its own gates inside its invocation and reports the result.
That report is an attestation, never a measurement -- v3 runs no per-task
orchestrator gate at all.
Outside the repository: per-task records pair a bug id with a file and a line,
which the publishing rule does not allow in a committed artefact.
This is also the run store. v3-state.json, tasks.jsonl, phases/, chunks/ and
patcher-report.json all live here, and --resume reads them. Nothing durable
in the repository points at this path, so archive the run before the disk
goes away -- the subset 2 run was lost exactly that way.
